title: Nimos (or Avnimos) the Weaver
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great philosopher among the sages of the nations of the world in the time of R' Meir. In [Chagigah 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.15b.15) he asked R' Meir: Does all wool that goes down into the cauldron come up? etc.[^2]

And in [Ruth Rabbah 2:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.2.13): Avnimos HaGardi's mother died, and Rabbi Meir went up to show him his face (to pay a condolence visit), and found them sitting as mourners. After a time his father died, and Rabbi Meir found them occupied in their work. He said to him: It seems to me that your mother is dearer to you than your father. He said to him: Is it not written, ‘a woman to her mother’s house’? He said to him: You have spoken well, for you have no father.[^3]

And in [Bereshit Rabbah 65:20](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.65.20), and in [Eichah Rabbah, Petichta 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah%2C_Petichta.2): Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: No philosophers have arisen in the world like Balaam son of Beor and like Avnimos HaGardi. And in [Shemot Rabbah 13:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.13.1): He asked our Sages, of blessed memory: How was the earth created at first? They said to him: Go to Abba Yosef the builder, etc.[^1]

notes.text: The notice abbreviates the exchange about creation. The sages direct the questioner to Abba Yosef the builder.

In the linked Chagigah, Nimos asks Rabbi Meir whether all wool that goes into the cauldron comes back out. The linked Shemot Rabbah names Avnimos explicitly as the person asking about creation, and has the Sages direct him to Abba Yosef the builder. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2713&lang=en) cites these accounts and records his own name conjecture.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 946) has Ruth Rabbah 2:13 and Bereshit Rabbah 65:20. The supplied Hebrew reads Bereshit Rabbah 2:13 and 65:2. In the linked Ruth passage the closing clause speaks of “a gentile,” where Hyman uses the second person. Both the linked Bereshit Rabbah and Eichah Rabbah give the philosophers’ comparison in Rabbi Abba bar Kahana’s name.
